[quote=technokratisches_kaiserreich;60030124][spoiler=[b]Counteroffensive[/b]]

The Hydronians completely misunderstand how JDAMs work. While theoretically, the jamming systems could block the GPS portions of the bomb, constant frequency hopping would quickly undermine the jamming conducted by the Hydronian systems. However, even if the Hydronians managed to jam the bombs, which would be highly unlikely, the bombs would still be able to hit their targets. The inertial navigation system (INS) of the JDAMs maintains its acceleration and direction using onboard sensors including accelerometers and gyroscopes. THEP satellites would be useless when attempting to interfere with the JDAMs. The coordinates of the refineries, pipelines, petrochemical factories, drills, strategic stockpiles and other oil infrastructure would be preprogrammed before launch. Even if in the extremely unlikely case they were forced to operate completely with INS, the bombs would still be able to drop within 30 meters of their targets. The GBU-37 JDAMs, weighing 5,000 lbs each would definitely still be able to eviscerate their targets due to their engineering and the extremely inept Hydronian defenses. The B-25EL strikes wouldnt be limited to just the oil infrastructure, however. Other B-25EL aircraft would move to destroy the Hydronian logistics behind their war effort. JDAMs would be dropped onto major Hydronian port facilities to target loading cranes, loading facilities and shipping lanes to hit major sealift capabilities. However, the main target would be Hydronian transportation systems. 5,000 lb JDAMs would be dropped onto key bridges, railway junctions and tunnels to choke the enemy's ability to move troops and supplies. B-25EL strikes would have the express purpose of destroying everything a modern military needs to function: oil for aircraft and vehicles, ports needed for sealift, food supplies for the troops, ammunition for their guns, and others. 

The Gunslinger and Rakete missiles were designed by Kaiserliche Maschinenwerke for the purpose of surviving in highly contested airspace. Through a variety of countermeasures the missiles make short work of the Hydronian interceptors sent after them. At supersonic speeds, the missiles travel at extremely fast speeds to rapidly reduce the amount of time given to the enemy interceptors to respond and chase them. Even if interceptors are able to respond, the high-G maneuvers of the missiles allow them to evade Hydronian attacks. The missiles are able to manipulate their aerodynamic surfaces to generate differential drag in order to make high speed maneuvers. Propulsion divert systems also help the missiles execute high-speed maneuvers in order to avoid interceptors. Its low radar cross section combined with radar absorbing materials would make it very hard for any interceptors to lock onto them and chase them down. Onboard jammers and ECMs also help the missile to jam enemy interceptors and utilize spoofing to create multiple fake targets to make the enemy missiles lock onto a ghost target. Even if all these methods fail the missiles are armed with a next generation defense system. The missile with missile defense idea created by Maschinenwerke would be put into full display in the skies over Hydronia. Directed energy weapons onboard the missiles would work to destroy any incoming interceptors along with smaller kinetic interceptors. After easily moving through the enemy's interceptors, the Gunslingers encounter the evasive maneuvers of the Hydronian jets attempting to desperately escape. However, this doesnt pose much of an obstacle to the Raketes and Gunslingers. The multitude of sensors: infrared, radar, CEC and electronic signals allow them to maintain a constant lock even on maneuvering aircraft. The aforementioned maneuvering capabilities allow the missiles to match and exceed the aircraft's evasive maneuvers. Big data algorithms trained based on thousands of air engagements including with Hydronia's aircraft allow the missiles to predict the movements of Hydronian aircraft allowing them to quickly close the gap. Ultimately, the Hydronians had overplayed their hand here. In a gamble to try to drive back the Kaiserreichs air support, they had made their aircraft sitting ducks to Reichswehr interceptors. 

You cant kill what you cant see was the philosophy behind the Reichswehrs loitering munition drones. Hydronian acoustic systems had failed miserably against the drones, forcing them to phase them out. However, their alternatives wouldnt prove significant improvements either. WIth radar off the table the Hydronians had tried to switch to optical and infrared. These might have been effective against a large, loud and gas burning aircraft but the drones would likely prove extremely hard to find. The small frames of the loitering munitions, just a couple inches across would make them extremely hard to spot with optical sensors. At the same time, their ability to blend into terrain using their camouflage would add yet another obstacle to optical tracking. The slow moving and hovering drones along with its erratic movements would make it even harder to identify amongst all the other moving objects in the wild: birds, falling leaves, etc. Infrared scanners would be even harder to use. The already extremely small infrared signal given off by the drones electronics would be blurred into an unrecognizable piece of data by the cooling systems onboard. Through these built in detection issues the drones would largely be unaffected by the Hydronian drones. With the radar systems of Hydronia largely destroyed the drones would move on to disrupt Hydronian conventional forces. At all times Hydronian vehicles, arms depots and soldiers would be targeted by the drones giving them no respite. The swarms of Hydronian drones would be quickly dealt with by the THOR systems. Through its high-powered microwaves it fries the electronics of the drones and to make them fall harmlessly onto the ground. However, the air bases that released the drones wouldnt go unharmed either. Tracking the signal between operators and the drones themselves the Reichswehr would quickly find the location of the air bases. With the exact locations, given away by the Hydronian signals, a series of ground based Donnerkeil cruise missiles would be launched towards the bases. 

The Hydronian return to their old tactics of diving deep underwater would be near suicidal. Attempting to outrange the massive amount of torpedoes fired from aircraft, helicopters, surface craft and submarines would be nearly impossible. The 50 kilometre range of the torpedoes would allow them to quickly reach the submarines at the bottom of the ocean (deepest point on Earth: 10km). Ultimately, by coming so close to the fleet, the Hydronians had given up their main defense of stealth. With that gone the overwhelming firepower of the Kaiserreich combined with the short range engagement gave the Reichswehr the tools to quickly finish them off. Even on top of the maneuvering capabilities of the torpedoes the sheer amount of torpedoes would make it highly unlikely for the ATTs to be able to intercept all of them(assuming the ATTs are carried by the subs, the fleet would obviously be able to carry much more torpedoes) allowing them to saturate the torpedo defenses. As they went, the Reichswehrs ASW helicopters would drop sonobuoys in the surrounding area. The Reichswehr had trapped the Hydronian subs and with the torpedoes hot on their tail, there was no way the Reichswehr would turn down such a good opportunity to cripple the Hydronian sub fleet. The sonobuys would provide constant tracking even if the enemy attempted to flee the area. With the submarines opening fire on them, the UUVs were serving their primary purpose: to drain the limited torpedo defense of the enemy while the main strike came. The UUVs utilizing their electronic engines would stay in pursuit of the enemy subs and start to catch up. Their much smaller frames would take up much less hydrodynamic drag allowing them to perform much tighter maneuvers and chase at higher speeds. All the while during the pursuit the UUVs would fire their torpedoes, and if any UUVs came close enough to the UUVs their proximity fuses would trigger to crush the hull of the subs. From the Kaiserliche Marine supply ships the cheap UUVs would be constantly dropped into the waters to reinforce the swarm. Even as the subs tried to save their supplies the UUVs would force them to fire. If they didnt the proximity fuses would trigger as the UUVs moved closer and closer and be used to crush the submarine's hulls. The Reichswehr had decided that they would ensure that the Hydronian submarines and their sailors would die here, buried under the waves.

Even as the Hydronian lines broke into full on retreat the J-16s wouldnt break their constant bombing. The vehicles and men pulling back en masse would make quick targets for the GBU-37 JDAMs. The 5,000 lb bombs would be used to hit the retreating vehicles and men as they tried to pull back. Cluster munitions would also be dropped onto the personnel as they pulled back to maximize casualties. 155 mm artillery guns would be used to pound the retreating men using the standard 22 km ranging round. Dropping submunitions, the artillery shells would be able to cover a large area of retreating troops and vehicles. Suicide drones would be released from the LCACs to chase down retreating troops and vehicles and detonate. IFVs would use their 30 mm autocannons to gun down retreating combatants using their high-explosive rounds. The Panzerkampfwagen Sturmfalke main battle tanks would fire their 130 mm rounds to fire on Hydronian armored vehicles. Their uranium tipped shells would be used to help breach through even heavily armored enemy vehicles. 

Sniperfire would be unlikely to be able to down drones on scale effectively. The fast moving, erratic and very small suicide drones would not only be very hard to spot but also extremely hard to shoot down. Against the backdrop, spotting the quiet and small drones themselves would be like picking out a needle from a haystack. Upon meeting thermal using Hydronian troops red phosphorous smoke would be released rendering their thermals near useless. Drones during gunfights would help augment the paratroopers by not only helping them blow up the enemy but also perform reconnaissance to find the enemies locations. The GPS jamming would have little effect on the JDAMs. Its internal INS along with preprogrammed coordinates would allow them to hit the Hydronian forces mere minutes after air support was called in. The paratroopers would continue this tactic, once engaging the Hydronians the JDAMs would be quickly called in. As they moved to sabotage the Hydronians, target coordinates would be called in to the Reichswehr jets who would then drop JDAMs onto the target. 

The Hydronians would make several critical mistakes in their counteroffensive that the Kaiserreich would rapidly deal with. First, the jets and helicopters would be the first targets. Bringing a large amount of jets and helicopters into heavily saturated airspace would be a massive strategic blunder only rivaled by the Hydronian navy's decisions off Nestorstaat. A large net of radar systems would help detect the incoming wave of aircraft and helicopters at long range. The AN/FPS-series along with AWACS help identify and track the large amount of incoming aircraft and helicopters. AWACS then helped manage the air defense from far behind the frontlines. The large amount of data on the incoming aircraft would be routed through a central battle management system including C2 nodes which assigns targets to the most suited air defense systems. Completely unsuppressed Reichswehr air defences would engage the enemy aircraft in a series of five layers. At the first layer, FAS-3 Rakete and Gunsligner interceptors move to intercept the incoming aircraft far before they are able to reach the Reichswehr forces. At 400 kilometres out the FAS-3 and Gunslingers become operational and carry out strikes on the incoming air forces (described the missile capabilities above). Even if the Hydronians were able to pass the first layer of interceptors the mid-ranged SAMs would engage at a range of 70 kilometres out. NASAMS would be activated against them. The networked system is made up of radar systems, a FDC, launcher units and electro-optical /infrared sensors. At over 100 kilometres the radar detects the incoming aircraft and helicopters with the data quickly being transferred to the FDC which tracks them and classifies threats based on altitude, speed, direction and type. Once the threats are locked onto the FDC assigns the best positioned launcher unit, distributed across Reichswehr held territory, to launch interceptor missiles. Through CEC and datalink the missile is able to accurately break through jamming and spoofing to intercept its target. If the aircraft and helicopters pass through both layers the third layer awaits them. SHORAD utilizing radars, electro-optical sensors and infrared scans the skies for incoming aircraft. At a distance of 30 kilometres the systems engage and fire their interceptor missiles. Utilizing CEC, datalink and onboard sensors the systems utilize a proximity fuse to explode near helicopters and aircraft. Finally, even if a small number of Hydronian aircraft managed to break through all three layers of air defense, the point defense systems would kick in. Armed with dual 20 mm gatling guns the point defenses fire at 5,000 rounds per minute at incoming threats along with its short range interceptors. If by some miracle the helicopters broke through all four layers of air defenses, somehow survived highly saturated airspace and unsuppressed air defense even more tools would be at the Reichswehrs disposal. MANPADS used by the Marineinfantriekorps would be used to mop up the last couple helicopters. Tracking the infrared signature of helicopter exhaust and engines the missiles quickly home into their locations. MANPAD operators hiding within the terrain engage the remaining helicopters. As the air defenses made short work of the incoming wave, that wouldnt be the only card up the Kaiserreich's sleeve. The J-15E air superiority aircraft through datalink would be connected to eight UAVs armed with Gunslinger, medium range air-to-air missiles and short range air-to-air missiles. This would give the Reichswehr two massive advantages over the Hydronian force: it would act as a force multiplier allowing the Reichswehr to outnumber the Hydronians despite having less manned aircraft as well as allowing manned aircraft to stay out of range of enemy fire. These UAVs, going ahead of the J-15Es are used to engage the enemy aircraft at long ranges, firing their payloads of before-visual-range air-to air missiles at the aircraft and helicopters. Ultimately, the Hydronian air force had played right into the Reichswehrs hands giving them almost every single advantage. They believed that they had superiority in numbers but this would be far from the case. The J-15E force multiplier would greatly expand the Reichswehr air presence, five layers of unsuppressed air defences would fire into the wave of aircraft while the Gunslingers and Raketes continued their work. Air superiority would remain firmly in Reichswehr hands, the reckless wave attack only served to increase Reichswehr pilots' confirmed kills. 

The point defense systems would make quick work of the incoming shells, destroying them before they are able to impact any important vehicles or infrastructure. With air superiority in their hands the Reichswehr would work to rapidly obliterate the Hydronian forces. Again, the Hydronians attempted to rely on numbers to try to overwhelm Kaiserreich forces but combined arms would help the Reichswehr to dismantle the counteroffensive. JDAMs would be dropped from J-16s as the large force tried to mobilize. Key bridges, railroads, highways, ports and other transportation infrastructure would be hit to throw a wrench into the Hydronian mobilization. As the large force moved towards the east, the Reichswehr controlled airspace above them would prove deadly. 5,000 lb GBU-37 JDAMs would be dropped constantly onto the enemy forces to target personnel, tanks and armored vehicles. 155 mm howitzers would pound the enemy forces with rocket assisted cluster munitions specifically designed to kill a large amount of soldiers over a large area. Suicide drones would be used against the enemy as well. The low-flying and cheap drones maintain a constant bombardment against the Hydronians. Personnel and armored vehicles would be targets for the suicide drones, armed with thermite to burn through the heavy tank armor. Sealift, now enabled by the Regent Kriecher G-12, would bring thousands of more Marineinfantriekorps troops onto the eastern side of Hydronia. By now the Reichswehr presence in the east would be slightly more than 85,000 troops. Armored divisions backed by heavy air support would continue to pour into Hydronian territory in the east.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Mainland operations[/b]]
The kaiserreich JDAMs, although clearly very advanced, would fall victim to Hydronia's jamming units and other EW capabilities for a variety of reasons. Frequency hopping is an unviable option for JDAM GPS systems, due to the limited amount of frequencies that GPS can operate on. The Hydronian jamming units can easily block all three GPS frequencies (L1, L2 and L5). With GPS disabled, the INS would begin to drift over longer distances, greatly reducing their accuracy. If the JDAMs did manage to find their way to their targets with any degree of accuracy, they would be easily shot down by Hydronia's laser-homing man portable missiles.

The enemy missile's High-G maneuvers would not be enough to shake the Hydronian missiles. Laser-homing would allow for a quick and accurate lock on the enemy missiles. This lock could then easily be kept due to lasers moving at the speed of light, allowing the missiles to receive data on the enemy's movements quickly and react accordingly. High speeds would also not prove effective, due to the before mentioned nature of lasers, providing Hydronia's missiles with the highest accuracy. The kaiserreich's ECMs would be ineffective against lasers and waste of time. Spoofing the missiles' lasers would be very difficult without a physical decoy. Since electronic spoofing doesn't produce a physical surface for the laser to bounce off of, the missiles wouldn't be deceived and would continue towards their targets. The kaiserreich jets' last line of defence, directed energy weapons would be effective, but only on a small scale. The energy weapons couldn't target and destroy every interceptor that the Hydronians deployed. Even if they could, it would provide the Hydronians with enough time to escape and regroup. If the enemy missiles managed to survive the interceptors, the Hydronian aircraft would be well on their way to regroup. The kaiserreich's data on Hydronian aircraft would be limited due to only having one other air engagement with them, over the skies of Nestorstaat. They would be ineffective in predicting the Hydronian's evasive maneuvers, further providing the aircraft with time to escape. Once the aircraft regrouped with the now 200 other aircraft in the sky, they would be easily able to defend themselves. Huge numbers of the interceptors could be fired as needed against the Kaiserreich missiles. It would be near impossible for them to survive.

The drones may have survived Hydronia's drone swarm attack, but the effectiveness of them would be thrown into question. It would be impossible for the drones to search across an entire country, especially noting Hydronia's size. The locations of every unit would be impossible to gather, due to camoflauge measures routinely used by the Hydronian army. Methods such as infrared would have more success, but Hydronian snipers would easily be able to shoot down the drones. A military-grade drone with enough firepower to cause serious damage would be heavy and bulky. This would slow it down and provide an easy target for Hydronia's well trained snipers. However, five travelling units would be outplayed by the drones, being bombed by them. The donnerkeils would be dealt with through a combination of chaff, jamming and flares.

The long-range enemy torpedoes had failed to account for one key point, Pressure. Every ~10m of depth increases the pressure by an extra ~1 atmosphere. The Hydronian submarines would be far more pressure-resistant than small torpedoes. By diving below maximum operational depth, the submarines would escape whilst the torpedoes would be slowly crushed behind them, removing the need to expend anymore ATTS. The UUVs would also suffer the same fate as the torpedoes. The submarines, now diving well below their safety limits would be safe from the UUVs being squashed under pressure. Even if the torpedoes and UUVs survived the pressure, the water density would cause their accuracy to falter, most likely causing them to sail straight past the submarines. The sonobuoys would be dealt with through a combination of torpedoes and electronic countermeasures. The submarines would fire a small amount of torpedoes to conserve their supplies. The hope would be to destroy the sonobuoys. If the torpedoes failed, jamming would ensure that the data collected by the sonobuoys could not be transmitted back to the Kaiserreich fleet.

C-RAM attached to armoured vehicles would attempt to cover the troops from artillery fire as they made their retreat to higher ground. The aim would be to intercept the artillery shells before they could release their submunitions. The C-RAM would also provide cover from the tank shells. Mobile Jamming units would be employed to disrupt the JDAMs GPS signals, causing their accuracy to deviate. The Hydronians would most likely have enough time to get out of the vicinity of the JDAMs, as well as inaccuracies due to lack of GPS. Otokar cobra I APCs bought from Indonocaismnic also help to provide cover, maintaining constant fire on the enemy troops and vehicles. Hydronias own cheap suicide drones would be put to use against the enemy drones. Released from trucks and ground-based launch pads behind the frontline, They would swarm around the enemy drones, distracting them from their targets. They would also be packed with cheap explosives, which would detonate upon crashing into enemy drones. Most Hydronian soldiers had already boarded the armoured vehicles, providing cover from the IFV fire.

Sniper fire may have failed, but Hydronia had more tricks up its sleeve. The versatile mobile jamming units would be used to disrupt the drones signals connecting them to the operator. The paratroopers couldnt use the drones if they couldnt talk to them. Additionally, the Kaiserreichs own use of red phosphorus smoke would hinder their drones efforts. Mere minutes would be enough time for the highly skilled Hydronian soldiers to vacate the vicinity of the JDAMs. After the first team fell victim to the bombs, the Hydronians quickly learned from their mistakes. They would make themselves seen by the paratroopers, causing them to call in the JDAMs, but by the time they had done so, The Hydronians were already escaping. Inaccurate guidance caused by GPS jamming would also cause the JDAMs to begin to deviate, further buying time for the Hydronians. The Red phosphorus smoke would hinder the paratroopers own efforts to vacate the JDAMs  target site. The Kaiserreich would be killing their own troops.

The gunslingers would be dealt with through the use of the same interceptor missiles as before. Their high-accuracy laser homing would soon lock onto the enemy missiles. This lock would be firm, only ridiculous and dangerous manoeuvres would shake them. The sheer number of these interceptors, being launched from at least 50 aircraft would ensure that they could not all be destroyed by the Kaiserreichs energy weapons. Once the gunslingers were destroyed, the jets would then move on to taking out the systems that launched them. Barrages of air-to-surface missiles would be launched, using infrared to home in on troops and launchers. The jets would now get to taking on the second layer. Air-to-surface missiles designed for long-range strikes would have a range far greater than that of the enemy SAMs, built for defensive purposes. The Hydronian strikes would have a range of up to 100km, allowing them to see and strike the SAMs and their radars using infrared before they had time to react. Even if the SAMs had time to target the missiles and fire, the sheer number of missiles would again come to Hydronias advantage, making it highly improbable that all missiles could be intercepted. The third layer of defences would be easy. The range of air-to-surface missiles would once again outdo the kaiserreich defences. The missiles have a maximum range of 100km, gatling guns couldn't match that. Again, rounds of laser-homing missiles would be fired, not all of them could be intercepted. The MANPADS would prove to be the greatest challenge. The front-running jets would take direct hits, but the helicopters, staying within a defensive formation, would be safe. A change of tactic would be required to deal with this threat, a risky one too. Flares could be used against the MANPADS, but only the attack helicopters possessed such capabilities. The helicopters would now take the lead on the attack, using their flares as a decoy, to lure the MANPADS away from the engine heat of the helicopters. If these failed, interceptor missiles would be used to take down the MANPAD missiles. The gunslingers had failed once before, and they would do again. laser-homing interceptors would again be launched in numbers to take on the enemy missiles, producing the same effects described earlier. Three more jets would be hit, but this would be but a pinprick to the aerial counterattack. Once the missiles were dealt with, the jets could easily take out the UAVs. Air-to-air missiles using infrared would easily see the vehicles and rocket towards them. The hastily put together air defences would prove no match for the powerful Hydronian counteroffensive. The armada of aircraft would now split into two groups. The first group, comprised of attack helicopters and jets, would begin taking out key enemy targets. The attack helicopters would use air-to-surface missiles to carry out precision strikes on radar, fuel tankers, air defence systems, captured transport links and other critical infrastructure in the kaiserreich's captured territory. The jets of the group would begin a brutal carpet bombing campaign across the territory, using high-yield gravity bombs. Nowhere would be safe. The second group would begin taking out targets in the sky. Air-to-air infrared homing missiles would be sent towards the J-16 and J-15Es, whilst laser-homing interceptors would be put on the ready for the enemy's resistance. At least 2 jets would target a single enemy jet at once, ensuring that numbers are on Hydronia's side.

Point defence systems would be key targets for Hydronia's precision strikes. Whilst the first round of artillery would be intercepted, the rounds that followed would be able to sail through the air into reichswehr controlled territory without resistance. Additionally, surface-to-surface missiles would be launched from man-portable missile launchers. The JDAMs would be dealt with using Hydronia's same old tactics of jamming. Portable jamming units would be able to disable the JDAMs GPS, whilst surface-to-air interceptors would attack the JDAMs. Their INS would drift over the long distance. The drift may not affect large industrial targets, but small units of men on the ground would easily have time to escape. Howitzers would cause heavy casualties despite Hydronian troops hiding behind hills to protect themselves, but the kaiserreich troops wouldn't be safe either. The continuing carpet bombing, artillery fire and surface-to-surface bombardment would be sure to inflict casualties. Suicide drones would be annoying to deal with. Their cheapness and high speed made the quite effective, but they would be prone to jamming. Hydronia's portable jamming units would cut off the drones from their operators, causing them to drop to the ground, where they could easily be dealt with. Hydronian numbers would rapidly increase, bringing total troop numbers up to ~100,000. This, combined with an abundance of armoured vehicles and tanks would begin to provide resistance to the reichswehr and push them back, although the primary purpose of these troop deployments were to hold their ground until karcovian help could arrive.

Away from the frontlines, in Seraphar, the state capital of Lumir, a total of 50,000 troops have been deployed, with more on their way. They will stand as a backup, in case the frontlines fail and the reichswehr reach the urban area.
[/spoiler]
